Ok, then please continue (this is a test whether we can operate that also from the Codex app).

Address the two issues in separate PRs, when done run the session recovery tool to fill in the resources used as to have a complete log.

I’ll resume the two PRs, using the 10% overlap limit. I’ll run token recovery after the work and import the completed-turn counts once each. The final active turn may need a recovery pass after it closes.

The preflight still flags the changed setup and lockfile fingerprints. I’ll recheck the runtime before using it. For the position PR, the reviewer’s exact list will set the disc datums—including 795 and 2328 mm; those are explicit choices, not the result of flooring the old values.
For the positioning PR, list in the PR by how much every disk has been moved in the PR description.
I’ll include a table for all 18 discs in the position PR, showing each old datum, new datum, and signed displacement.

The position controls pass, including checks that the first-disc shift is applied only once. The ACTS runtime imports also pass. I’ll use the PDF skill to inspect the reviewed table and figure while the revised DD4hep and Geant4 checks run.

The position build passed all six CTests, with zero overlaps, and Geant4 initialized with all 14,858 sensitive paths.

The first concentric single-chip layouts reduce overlap substantially, but still miss the 10% ceiling. I’m now testing alternative arrangements with explicit polygon coverage checks, so uncovered gaps remain visible.

I’ll include all 18 discs in the positioning PR description, with their previous position, new position, and signed displacement. I’ll use the implemented geometry as the baseline, including the first disc’s existing 3.5 mm shift.

The positioning geometry has passed all six native build checks and Geant4 initialization. I’m finishing the movement table and regression checks. The disc overlap study is still in progress: the first concentric single-chip layout exceeds 10%, so it hasn’t passed the selection criteria.

[PR #40](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/40) is open with the full 18-disc movement table. All 137 module-layout regression tests passed.

A Cartesian single-chip tiling with an inner polar ring brings projected overlap below 10%, but it extends beyond the current support envelope. I’m checking physical clearance, displaced-vertex coverage, and service space before judging whether it is a viable proposal.

The candidate now uses 328 single-chip modules per disc, compared with 448 chips in the existing quads. It measures 8.91% projected silicon overlap overall and 9.91% within the unchanged active annulus. Polygon containment checks passed for straight rays from on-axis vertices across −150 to +150 mm on all 18 discs.

It still needs engineering review: the module envelope reaches about 210 mm radius, and the inherited shared service trunk fails the estimated packing check. I’ll make those limits explicit in the design PR.

ACTS passed the updated audit: 324 matched tracks for each layout and six exhaustive control tracks agreed with the finite-surface oracle, with zero mismatches. The overlap and body checks also pass at every disc distance.

I’ve run usage recovery for the completed app turns. This active turn’s final counters become available after it closes, so they still need a follow-up recovery pass.

Both PRs are open: [#40 for positioning](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/40) and [#41 for disc optimization](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/41). PR #40 includes every disc’s signed movement. PR #41 includes the coverage proof, ACTS checks, figures, and failed service-space estimates.

PR #40’s initial hosted checks passed. I’m waiting for the updated logger commit and PR #41’s hosted checks to finish.

Both PRs’ final hosted checks passed. The positioning description has all 18 displacements, and the optimization PR states the guard and service-design conditions clearly.

I’m arranging one follow-up recovery pass after this turn closes so the resource log includes its final token counters.
The scheduler rejected the first single-run timing rule. I’m checking a corrected schedule for the final token backfill; both PRs and their validation are already complete.

Created both PRs:

- [#40 — positioning](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/40): description lists all 18 discs’ old/new positions and signed movements.
- [#41 — optimization](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/41): meets the 10% geometric target with coverage and ACTS evidence. Guard qualification and failed service packing remain explicit engineering limits.

Both hosted checks passed. Completed-turn usage is logged; one follow-up is scheduled to recover this turn’s final tokens after it closes.
